sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2025:Ahc:95962-Db
Court No. - 43
Case :- Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. - 12070 of 2025

Petitioner :- Shobhit Chaturvedi
Respondent :- State Of Uttar Pradesh And 2 Others

Counsel for Petitioner :- Ashok Kumar Tripathi
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble J.J. Munir,J.
Hon'ble Praveen Kumar Giri,J.
Heard Mr. P.C. Srivastava, learned Counsel for the petitioner at substantial length in support of the
motion to admit this petition to hearing.

The allegation against the petitioner, Shobhit Chaturvedi is that he purchased a Beretta Pistol bearing No. B61214 W Caliber 7.65mm without any valid documents of purchase by his vendor and during investigation, he did not produce documents of his vendor's purchase.

The petitioner's first licence bearing No. 16439 is for a NPB revolver issued in the State of Uttarakhand and the second licence is for a single barrel breech loading gun bearing No. 1109 which too was secured from the District Magistrate on incorrect information where the applicant's original place of birth was shown as Agra instead of Lucknow.
Likewise, in column No.13 of the application, the particulars of the first licence have not been indicated though he had a licence.

In column No.11, which requires Shobhit Chaturvedi vs State Of Uttar Pradesh And 2 Others on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179021383/
1 information about licences in the family and his own

sentences.text: , he has not indicated his first licence issued from the State of Uttarakhand.
It is on these allegations that the present F.I.R. has been registered for offences punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 I.P.C. and sections 3, 25, 30 Arms Act.

There is also an allegation against the petitioner regarding the collusion with one Sanjay Kumar,
Arms Clerk in the Office of District Magistrate, Agra.
We must remark here that this kind of collusion between the Arms Clerk and the petitioner cannot come about without the participation of superior officers.

Looking to the allegations where a firearm of unknown origin of purchase has been secured which may be contrary to the terms of the licence permitted to the petitioner, besides furnishing of incorrect information in the application for the second firearm licence, we are not inclined to quash the impugned F.I.R. or interdict the ongoing investigation.
It would be open to the petitioner to avail his remedies of bail and/or anticipatory bail, if so advised.
Subject to the above remarks, this petition is dismissed.
Order Date :- 9.6.2025

Karan/Gaurav Kuls (Praveen Kumar Giri, J.) (J.J. Munir, J.)
